expects.rule: Content is written in plain language that most users understand: more than 4 in 10 adults struggle with public health content, and more than 6 in 10 when it includes numbers and statistics. Test with people of low health literacy.
The service meets WCAG 2.2 and is accessible to everyone who needs it, not only on desktop.
Text meets WCAG AA contrast: 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (18 pt or 14 pt bold), which also matters for the calm pastel palettes common in wellness.
Pages are short and scannable: visitors read about 20% of the words, and stressed visitors skim for the answer.

The first screen gives a way to act on the main need: book, call, start an assessment or download, with phone number and address visible for a clinic. NN/g found appointment scheduling the most frequent online healthcare task.
Clinicians are named with photo, credentials and specialty, and treatments and prices are listed in plain words.
Privacy, how health data is stored and used, and what the product is not (not a diagnosis, not emergency care) are stated in plain words and linked from the first screen.
Claims about results cite a figure and a source, with no before-and-after promises.

traits: 3 of 8 first screens are a full-bleed photograph or video of a person or medical object (Institute of Health, Rejuvenation Dentistry, Function); 2 show phone or dashboard screens (Bevel, Impilo); Pomegranate and Heva show none.

One main action on the first screen on 6 of 8 (Download App, Start testing, Request Demo, Register your interest, Get services, Learn More); only Rejuvenation Dentistry shows three (virtual consultation, book, phone).
The headline is 10 words or fewer at 51 to 104 px on 7 of 7 sites that have one (Health+ has none), in plain language (Check your health., Vitality, refined.).
4 of 8 pair a serif or display face for the headline with a plain sans for the rest (Heva, Function, Health+, Pomegranate); 2 use a single sans.
Backgrounds: 4 of 8 pale or cream (#f3f6f7, #fffaf0, #fdfdf1, #fef9ef), 2 photographic and dark, 2 saturated blue (Impilo, Health+ header).
Trust figures appear on the first screen on 4 of 8: rating count (Bevel 4.8 from 64.7k), counters (Institute of Health), lab tests and price (Function), HSA/FSA eligibility.
5 of 8 show a cookie or consent box over the first screen, which hides part of the layout.

sites.name: Bevel Health
sites.why: Pale blue (#f3f6f7) sky-gradient page: 75 px two-line headline 'Your Connected Health Coach' in a system sans-serif, one subtitle, a black App Store badge, '4.8 / 64.7k ratings', then an iPhone and a watch cut by the fold. Cookie box at bottom left.

sites.name: Institute of Health
sites.why: Full-bleed dimmed video of a blood-pressure cuff on a shoulder; 51 px headline at bottom left in Lay Grotesk, three counters at right (966 course units, 46 countries, 21 laboratory tests), Student Login and a Learn More tile. Grey (#e6e6e6) and white text.

sites.name: Pomegranate Health
sites.why: Cream (#fffaf0) page inside stacked pink and burgundy rounded tabs; 76 px headline 'Your personal health intelligence platform' in a rounded display face (Gliker), a four-line paragraph, 'Register your interest' button. No photograph; separate entries for individuals, employers and professionals.

sites.name: Rejuvenation Dentistry
sites.why: Header with name, 'Virtual Consultation', 'Book a Visit' and the phone number, a dark brown (#2c1910) menu of seven treatment links, then a black-and-white close-up photograph of the dentist behind the headline 'Dentistry Designed for Your Whole Body', address and name in small caps.

sites.name: Heva Health
sites.why: Page loads with an overlay on pale green (#fdfdf1): a 30% discount offer, a 104 px light condensed serif headline (PP Editorial New) and an email field with 'Continue'. The page behind has Care, How It Works, a HSA/FSA badge and clinician headshots lower down. Dark green (#39442b) text.
sites.recognition: Awwwards Site of the Day and Developer Award, 2024-07-26

sites.name: Function Health
sites.why: Full-bleed photograph of a woman in profile in a desert at dusk, 'Check your health.' in a light display serif (Financier Display) at 77 px, three figures (160+ lab tests, whole body, $1 per day), cream pill 'Start testing' in the header. Cookie box covers the left.

sites.name: Impilo
sites.why: Saturated blue-violet page: 82 px white headline 'Making at home healthcare easy.' in Gilroy with 'easy.' in cyan, line drawings of a thermometer and watch, and a dashboard card of blood-pressure data cut at the fold. 'Request Demo' pill in the header.

sites.name: Health+ Polyclinic
sites.why: Blue (#1f519c) header with a menu for clients and for health professionals, a 'Get services' button and 'Client zone'; a blurred photo of a magazine rack with three tiles (Health Care, 4 branches in Prague, Our Programs). Set in Inter with a serif for titles. Cookie box over it.

avoid: Stock photos of smiling doctors and a stethoscope, or a generic blue and white medical template.
Pale grey text on pastel backgrounds under 4.5:1 contrast to look calm.
Medical jargon and long paragraphs on the first screen, with no plain-language summary.
Before-and-after or miracle claims with no figure, source or clinician name.
Booking only through a form with no phone number, address or opening hours.
Opening a chat widget or newsletter pop-up before the visitor has read anything.
Hiding prices, data use and privacy behind a sign-up, or implying a diagnosis the product cannot give.
